target_transition.classification: Conditional reconstruction target; the exact incident RAM word, action, velocity, and TTC speed were not directly observed.

writer_families.family: ordinary airborne integration and floor collision
writer_families.incident_result: ACT_FREEFALL calls perform_air_step with AIR_STEP_CHECK_LEDGE_GRAB only. It does not enable AIR_STEP_CHECK_HANG. Ordinary integration moves downward from vy=-20; floor assignments use a queried or retained floor, not an unrelated upper coordinate.
The ledge floor query is capped by next_y + 160, so it cannot produce a 3155.25-unit rise.

The snap to ceilHeight-160 requires AIR_STEP_CHECK_HANG, upward ceiling contact, ACT_START_HANGING, A held, and a referenced hangable ceiling. ACT_FREEFALL omits the hang check; the reconstructed state is descending and its ceiling is far above.
The only direct upward adjustment is 20-2*actionTimer, at most 20 units.

Platform oVelY is never applied. Mario's Y changes only in the angular-rotation branch. The incident spinner has zero angular velocity under TTC_SPEED_STOPPED, so its vertical platform displacement is exactly zero.

The only reachable retained pointers in the incident grid are NULL and persistent spinner slot 46. The spinner does not unload or reuse its slot. All 65,536 counterfactual fast-spinner phases remained below 21.377 units; the stopped incident spinner produces zero.

writer_families.family: object interaction, pole, cannon, whirlpool, and attachment snaps
writer_families.incident_result: These paths require a matching interaction or automatic/submerged action and a valid used-object pointer. None matches the reconstructed freefall state or nearby red-coin/spinner objects in the bounded synthetic searches.

writer_families.family: warp, spawn, cutscene, and area initialization
writer_families.incident_result: These relocate Mario only with a level/area or cutscene transition, which is absent from the continuous incident footage and action state.

When find_floor returns NULL, update_mario_geometry_inputs copies marioObj->header.gfx.pos into MarioState.pos and queries the floor again. Static analysis found no legal TTC-native path that can leave graphical Y approximately 3155.25 units above physical Y: TTC moving surfaces update their own object graphics, platform displacement updates MarioState, shell offsets are only +42/+45, and water-only offsets are at most +60 plus a type-level bob bound below 148. A renderer prevObj/flame transform and an ending-cutscene floor assignment can independently change graphical Y, but both are non-TTC/action-gated.

runtime_probe.assessment: The compiled JP libsm64 branch legally propagates an arbitrary injected graphical/physical position divergence. No branch execution occurred in the bounded stopped-clock controller-only bootstrap run. Neither result supplies a natural producer of the required divergence or an incident-compatible precursor.

writer_families.incident_result: Clearing bit 24 of the 32-bit IEEE-754 Y word produces y/4 exactly and reproduces the upper floor and landing trajectory. No byte or halfword writer to Mario Y appeared in native traced execution.

bounded_conclusion: The enumerated arithmetic, collision, platform, interaction, transition, and graphical-position writer paths do not produce the conditional 3155.25-unit target in the tested native domains or static matched-ROM source analysis. The floor-null graphical-position copy can propagate an injected incident-scale graphical/physical divergence, but the stopped-clock controller-only probe recorded zero branch executions in 4096 updates and no TTC-native producer of the required divergence was found. The unresolved independent graphical writers are non-TTC renderer-prevObj/flame and ending-cutscene cases. The three exact reachable, synthetic no-flip, and synthetic bit-clear render sequences have been compared with the VOD, but all scene and screen-space-motion results remain indeterminate because cross-domain positive controls and dense transition localization are absent. Direct mutation of MarioState Y is the only tested input that reproduces the conditional numeric transition and subsequent synthetic trajectory; graphical-position corruption through an unknown software or hardware initiator remains unproven.
